    Getting started

    This walkthrough builds Home → Settings and then routes Settings back through a shared Home destination.

    1. Author the UXML

    Create two NavElement roots and place a NavButton inside Home.

    <ui:UXML xmlns:ui="UnityEngine.UIElements"
         xmlns:nav="NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Elements">
    <nav:NavElement name="home" view-category="Demo" view-key="Home">
        <nav:NavButton text="Settings"
                       signal-category="Demo" signal-key="OpenSettings" />
    </nav:NavElement>
    <nav:NavElement name="settings"
                    view-category="Demo" view-key="Settings" />
</ui:UXML>

    2. Register addresses

    Open Tools > UI Navigation > Key Catalog and add:

    Tab Address
    View Demo / Home
    View Demo / Settings
    Signal Demo / OpenSettings

    Assign these addresses in UI Builder and save the UXML.

    3. Build the graph

    1. Create and open a UI Navigation Graph.
    2. Configure Home to Show Demo/Home and Hide Demo/Settings on enter.
    3. Add a Database Signal output Demo/OpenSettings and connect it to Settings.
    4. Configure Settings to Show Demo/Settings and Hide Demo/Home.
    5. Add a Custom Signal output Home on Settings.
    6. Create Send Signal, set Address Type = Custom and Custom Signal = Home, then connect the Settings output to its Multi Enter.
    7. Create a Portal with Type = Signal, Signal Address = Custom, Custom Signal = Home, and connect its output to Home.
    8. Save the graph.

    The Settings output does not need a special Destinations port. Its existing Signal output connects directly to Send Signal.

    4. Connect the runtime

    Add one enabled UINavigatorBehaviour, assign the graph, and ensure the UXML is attached to a Player-context panel. Optionally add UIBackInputRouter for Escape, Backspace, and mouse Back/Forward.

    In Play Mode, NavButton opens Settings. Sending Custom Home reaches Send Signal, resolves the matching Portal, and enters Home. Application code can request the same route with Signal.Send("Home").
